title: Miso Ramen Bar
shortDescription: Chicken broth miso ramen with tofu and vegetables for ten
subtitle: Chicken broth miso ramen with tofu and vegetables for ten
description: Chicken broth simmers with aromatics, then finishes with red and white miso for a savory bowl base. Serve with ramen noodles, shredded chicken, seared tofu, bean sprouts, corn, and soft eggs.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Miso Ramen Bar in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Use green onions as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Simmer chicken broth
steps.instruction: Poach chicken thighs in broth with ginger and garlic 25 minutes until cooked through. Remove chicken, shred, and reserve. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Finish miso base
steps.instruction: Keep broth at a gentle simmer. Remove from heat, whisk white and red miso until dissolved, then return to low heat without boiling.

steps.title: Sear tofu
steps.instruction: Pat tofu dry, sear in oil until golden on multiple sides. Hold warm with shredded chicken. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 165°F on an instant-read thermometer. Plan about 12 minutes for this step at crew scale. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts.

steps.title: Set the bar
steps.instruction: Line up sprouts, corn, eggs, scallions, tofu, and chicken in hotel pans. Keep broth hot in a large pot. Plan about 15 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Miso Ramen Bar onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Assemble bowls
steps.instruction: Cook noodles, divide into bowls, ladle miso broth over, and let crews pick toppings. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: A splash of sesame oil at the bowl station adds aroma without changing the batch.
Spinach wilted in broth for 30 seconds adds green without extra pans.
Keep extra miso paste slurry nearby if broth needs salt at service.
tonightSpread: Miso ramen bar with tofu, chicken, eggs, and chili crisp.
Edamame with flaky salt for a simple side.
leftovers: Broth reheats gently—do not boil or miso flavor dulls.
Shredded chicken becomes lettuce wraps with miso dressing.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Miso ramen comes together faster than tonkotsu but still feels special. Tofu and chicken together keep vegetarians and meat eaters happy without cooking two separate meals.
mealPrepNotes: Never boil miso—whisk in off heat to preserve flavor. Prep all toppings before noodles go in. Chili crisp at the line is mandatory for half the hall.
